subject: art-design

moments.title: Lascaux cave paintings
moments.body:
Hundreds of images of aurochs, horses and deer cover the limestone walls of Lascaux, painted by lamplight with mineral pigments and reed brushes.

The caves were discovered by four teenagers in September 1940.
moments.takeaway: Image-making is at least as old as agriculture, perhaps older.

moments.title: Chauvet earlier still
moments.body: Chauvet's lions, rhinoceroses and bears push the archaeological date of figurative painting back by tens of millennia.
moments.takeaway: What counts as the 'beginning' of art keeps moving as new caves are dated.

moments.title: Picasso visits Lascaux
moments.body: After visiting the newly discovered cave, Picasso reportedly remarked that modern artists had 'invented nothing'.
moments.takeaway: The deep past can rebuke claims of modern originality.

now.title: Prehistoric art today
now.body: Replica caves (Lascaux IV, 2016) protect the originals while opening them to visitors. Pigment analysis and 3D scanning continue to refine dating.
now.open_questions: What did these paintings mean to those who made them, and can we ever know?

reflection: Cave painting is the oldest continuous human visual tradition we know.
